sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Dauphin County, Pennsylvania?
sections.html:
Two county offices share the work from the Administration Building at 2 South Second Street in Harrisburg. The Office of Tax Assessment sets and maintains assessed values and can be reached at (717) 780-6101, and the Tax Claim Bureau collects delinquent real estate tax at (717) 780-6125. Both keep weekday hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., though the Bureau accepts payments only until 4:00 p.m.

Current year bills do not come from the county building. The county's 39 municipalities pass unpaid accounts to the Bureau through their own tax collectors or treasurers. Ask the County Treasurer's office or your municipal office who collects the current bill for your address.

The county, a municipality and a school district all levy on the same parcel, so one bill combines three rates.

sections.h2: How high are property tax rates in Dauphin County?
sections.html:
The county's January 2026 millage sheet shows a county rate of 9.193 mills in every district, a 0.35 mill library rate in most, and then municipal and school rates that vary. Totals range from about 27.8 mills in Middle Paxton Township to 58.97 mills in Highspire Borough. The sheet also says that assessment ratios in all of Dauphin County, Harrisburg included, are 100%.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Dauphin County assessment?
sections.html:
File with the Board of Assessment Appeals after June 1 and no later than 4:30 p.m. on August 1. The board's rules reject any appeal that arrives after that date, even one that was mailed before it.

A separate rule covers a new or changed assessment during the year: the appeal must be received within 40 days of the date on the change notice. The Board sits at the Administration Building, second floor, and mail goes to PO Box 1295, Harrisburg, PA 17108-1295. The Board's phone is (717) 780-6102.

  • Appeals fall into five forms: single family residential, residential multi-family or apartment, farm, commercial or industrial, and exempt.
  • The owner, an authorized representative or a lessee who pays the tax must sign. A corporation signs through an officer.
  • A filing fee is due for every parcel, by check or money order to the Board, and it is never refunded.
  • The Board will not accept or hear an appeal while delinquent taxes remain on the parcel.
  • Only a Pennsylvania attorney may represent an owner before the Board, and the aggrieved party is expected to appear at the hearing.

Ask the Board for the fee amount that applies to your property class.

sections.h2: What happens when Dauphin County property tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
The account moves to the Tax Claim Bureau, which collects delinquent real estate tax for the county, the municipalities and the school districts. The Bureau began taking payments on 2025 delinquent tax on February 3, 2026, and it adds a $20 fee per tax due.

The Bureau accepts cash, certified checks, cashier's checks and money orders, and it takes cards online or by phone at a 2.55% fee, or $4.00 for Visa debit. Personal and business checks are returned. Not receiving a notice does not excuse the tax, and owners are responsible for keeping their mailing address current with the Tax Assessment Office.

Several taxing districts are collected elsewhere. Portnoff Law Associates handles Steelton Borough and the Steelton-Highspire School District from the 2018 tax, and Highspire Borough and Lower Paxton Township from the 2024 tax. CGA Law Firm handles Penbrook Borough from the 2024 tax. A Lower Paxton or Highspire owner with back tax should call the right collector first.

The Bureau also runs upset sales, judicial sales and the repository of unsold properties.

sections.h2: How do I sell a Dauphin County house when taxes are owed?
sections.html:
Order a tax certification before listing. The Bureau issues an official letter stating whether delinquent tax is due on a parcel, with a claim statement showing the amount as of that date, for $15 per parcel.

  • Pay the back tax at closing or before it, so the title company can issue clear title.
  • Ask for a tax sale abstract only if a sale has already happened. It costs $25 per parcel, per sale, and lists the notices and the purchaser.
  • Pay the Bureau by certified funds when the amount is large, since personal checks are not taken.
  • Confirm with the municipal collector whether current year tax is paid, because that bill is separate from the Bureau's.

Settling the balance before a sale keeps the Bureau from moving the parcel toward an upset sale, which is how the Bureau handles unpaid accounts.

sections.h2: What new rule affects landlords selling in Dauphin County?
sections.html:
Act 29 of 2026, House Bill 858, created a county maintained contact registry for non-owner-occupied property. It took effect September 18, 2026, after being signed July 20, 2026, and owner-occupied principal residences are exempt.

An owner of a rented or vacant property must give the assessment office a name, address, phone number and email for a person authorized to fix code violations. The first filing is due within 30 days of taking ownership, updates are due within 30 days of a change, and a failure to comply can bring a $500 fine. Lenders can be covered after a sale or foreclosure.

The Tax Assessment office takes the Act 29 owner contact form by mail, by email or in person, so a landlord who sells should file the update or confirm the new owner has done so.

sections.h2: What does the Dauphin County housing picture look like?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimates 293,351 residents in July 2025 across 524.87 square miles, with 129,660 housing units. The median value of an owner occupied home is $236,400 for 2020 to 2024, and 63.1% of homes are owner occupied.

Median household income is $76,242, median gross rent is $1,217, and the poverty rate is 13.0%. Black residents make up 19.3% of the population and Hispanic or Latino residents 13.8%.

With assessment ratios listed at 100%, a house assessed at the $236,400 median would owe roughly $7,300 at a 31 mill total. The real number depends on the district.

faqs.q: When is the deadline to appeal a Dauphin County assessment?
faqs.a: August 1 at 4:30 p.m. is the cutoff for annual appeals, and filing opens June 1. A late appeal is rejected even if mailed on time. Changed assessments during the year have a 40 day window from the notice date.

faqs.q: What is the county property tax rate in Dauphin County?
faqs.a: The county rate is 9.193 mills in every district on the January 2026 sheet, with a 0.35 mill library rate in most. Municipal and school rates are added, so district totals run from about 27.8 to 58.97 mills.

faqs.q: Who collects delinquent property tax in Dauphin County?
faqs.a: The Tax Claim Bureau collects it, with a few exceptions. Portnoff Law Associates and CGA Law Firm handle certain boroughs and Lower Paxton Township. The Bureau adds a $20 fee per tax due when it accepts payment.

faqs.q: How much is a tax certification in Dauphin County?
faqs.a: A tax certification costs $15 per parcel. It states whether delinquent real estate tax is due, and a claim statement shows the balance as of the certificate date. A sale abstract is a separate $25 per parcel.

faqs.q: Does Act 29 of 2026 apply to me?
faqs.a: It applies if you own non-owner-occupied property such as a rental or vacant house. You must register contact details with the assessment office within 30 days of ownership. Owner-occupied principal residences are exempt.
